summary: Backend-only (pure Python desktop tool) review and testing of AwakeToggle v17 features: random long breaks mid-session (minimize/restore own windows), chained sessions without gap (configurable %), tab-limit scoped to own tabs via UIA. Ran full existing suite (137 tests, all pass), reviewed logic in browse.py, core.py, browse_runner.py, config.py, and added 11 adversarial pytest tests covering edge cases (abort during break with minimized leftovers, force vs chain interplay, config boundary values, foreign-tab-only windows staying open, break reset after taken, extremes of pause range). Final result: 148/148 passed.
critical_code_review_comments: browse_runner.py _do_break safely bails via _check('break') -> Abort if stack is empty (self._opened True but _stack empty), so top = own[-1] cannot IndexError in practice. Verified.

core.py _tick consumes both force and chain in one tick; force bypasses USER_ACTIVE but chain only triggers on WAIT (i.e. last input was own), so user activity cannot cause auto-chain. Correct per spec.

browse_runner.py _tabs: fresh-tab attribution uses len(fresh) <= len(self._tab_events) to decide own vs foreign; this is pessimistic (treats surplus as foreign) and matches spec. OWN_TAB_GRACE_S expiry prunes stale events.
browse.py make_scenario pause_at range: randint(max(1, n//4), max(1, n*3//4)); for very small n this could degenerate but tests confirm 1 < idx < len(plan.steps)-1 across 200 seeds.
config.py validate for break_minutes/every_minutes requires lo<=v[0]<=v[1]<=hi — correctly rejects reversed/out-of-range tuples.
After abort during long break, minimized own windows remain minimized; _cleanup_leftover on next run calls _close_top which activates (restores) then closes. Verified by new adversarial test.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Pure Python desktop tool under /app/awaketoggle. Ignore /app/backend and /app/frontend template folders. Windows-only modules (win32.py, tabs_win.py, power_win.py, session.py, consent_win.py, badge_win.py) cannot be imported on Linux; UIA/desktop is simulated by FakeDesk/TabDesk fixtures in tests/test_browse.py and tests/test_v17.py. Run: `cd /app && python -m pytest -q tests`. v17 features (long breaks, chaining, own-tab tracking) are implemented correctly and well-covered.
